title: A K256 shared operand on B300 needs four K64 TMA boxes before four warp-local MMA partials can be emitted
backend: native_cuda warp MMA proposal; CuTe-DSL and native tcgen05 single-box routes remain separate
executor_revision: sm_103a@b00b2b8fda331011cad519d2817804ee7951fab3; external broker-bound diagnostic scripts, not a formal Executor receipt

evidence.note: The K64-box TMA and four-warp mma.sync prototype produced bitwise-equal complete outputs on both short-K shapes across five input distributions, with every input preserved. The prototype is outside the Compiler.

Under one broker-exclusive CUPTI comparison, the TMA prototype, selected-load Triton and official CAKE medians were 3.392, 5.856 and 3.040 microseconds. All five round outputs matched bitwise, each arm launched one kernel, and each arm's maximum within-round CV was below 5%. This is a custom diagnostic, not formal Evaluation admission.
The alternate single K256 TMA descriptor was refused by cuTensorMapEncodeTiled with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE before kernel launch. Its report cannot be used as a performance result.

The previous equality check rejected a K64 descriptor for a K256 shared staging buffer. The proposed structural rule admits only boxes that exactly match the buffer or evenly tile its final shared-memory axis. The existing CuTe and native tcgen05 emitters explicitly refuse the tiled route.

A swapped A/B TMA prototype retained exact bits across both short-K shapes and five input distributions while keeping the output register axes in public row-major order. Its B16 native/selected-Triton/official medians were 3.393/5.888/3.040 microseconds, with all three maximum within-round CVs below 5%. B1 official CV exceeded 5%, so its latency is descriptive.

The existing k_ranges canonicalizer merges adjacent ranges and erases four equal K partitions. A separate k_partitions field preserves ordered warp-local FP32 partials and their left-associated sum; common verification accepts the complete staged Schedule while current emitters refuse it by name.

observation: The B300 gap is partly an emission-mechanism gap. Direct selected-K loads reduced the largest historical TinyGEMM slowdown, but the two short-K fixtures remain slower than official CAKE. A scalar global-to-shared warp-MMA prototype was numerically exact yet much slower. Replacing its copies with four K64 TMA boxes made the B16 prototype nearly match the official kernel. A K256 box is rejected by the device API, so describing K256 staging with one K256 descriptor is not a valid shortcut. The existing common verifier's exact box/staging equality prevented the K64-box plan even before backend admission. Swapping the MMA operand orientation preserves bitwise outputs on both short-K fixtures and makes the accumulator axes match the public row-major output, avoiding a new output-layout abstraction. The existing k_ranges field merges adjacent intervals, so it cannot name the four distinct warp partials; that requires a separate typed K-partition commitment.
proposed_change: Admit a declared TMA descriptor box that evenly tiles the final axis of one shared staging buffer, while each existing emitter refuses a route it cannot emit. Then add a bounded native_cuda mma.sync path whose Schedule declares the four compute groups, four producer groups per operand, K256 stage and K64 descriptor boxes, named readiness/synchronization, four FP32 partials, CTA reduction and BF16 bias epilogue. Preserve exact target and bitwise Workload gates; do not route by operator name or copy the external kernel into the backend. A formal B300-M4 comparison also needs an Executor successor that accepts the existing broker's own admission receipt without inventing GPUQ_JOB_ID. Add ordered k_partitions to the MMA data model with complete nonoverlapping coverage, one execution group per partition, and instruction-aligned boundaries; keep every current emitter refusing it until the native warp-MMA route exists.
